name: bm-v4-junction-bending
claim: Junction bending is a released feature (NC1 angle k=4.0 @180°, plus 7S angles), not a new ingredient. HOW it is applied decides whether it yields a usable modulus. Our original as-formed `fix restrain` (pinned on AFTER assembly) is ill-conditioned — sign-flipping, no reproducible value. The FAITHFUL path (2026-10-02), creating real harmonic angles as the crosslinks form so the network equilibrates with them active (matching the released bond/react templates), yields a POSITIVE, well-conditioned, reproducible modulus. So the released model is not floppy once the angles are faithfully active; its modulus is finite and strongly density-dependent.
experiment: Implement bending via LAMMPS `fix restrain` pinned to each junction's as-formed angle (a per-junction rest angle, so no single-rest-angle frustration), with an auto-reduced timestep for stability. Measure the athermal modulus by energy minimisation (change_box + minimise; deterministic) and sweep the bending stiffness bending_k.
result: Three ways of applying the released NC1 bending (k=4.0), 3 seeds each at the corrected params: central-force (angles off) E per-seed −0.54/−1.32/−1.14 (consistent with zero); as-formed `fix restrain` 0.9/−2.53/−0.47 (ill- conditioned, sign-flipping); REAL angles created during assembly 36.7/27.6/37.5 LJ — positive, same sign, reproducible. The angle-during- assembly fix resolves the ill-conditioning. The modulus is strongly density- dependent (≈79 Pa at 2.9 crosslinks/rod → ≈7 Pa at 1.0/rod). Per-angle deletion is now implemented (delete-all + recreate on break), so the stiff network also REMODELS in the viscous hold — giving a reproducible remodelling time (τ ≈ 40 τ, bm-v1) alongside the modulus. Assembly stays make-only because make+break at this scale is too sparse to percolate (≈0.18/rod); matching the released dense make+break balance needs the authors' dense initial config + GCE.

purpose.question: Does junction bending yield the measurable modulus the vertex model needs?
purpose.mechanism: Bending constraints at crosslink junctions lift a sub-isostatic (z < 4) central-force network out of the floppy regime — the physically-expected rigidity source for a semiflexible fiber network.
purpose.expected_outcome: A finite, positive modulus that rises with bending stiffness. Observed: a large response, but not a reproducible modulus at v1 size.

key_assumptions: Bending = harmonic angle restraint pinned to each junction's as-formed angle (fix restrain).
Stiff restraints need a reduced timestep (dt ≈ 0.002; the spec's own regime).
Athermal (T=0) energy minimisation gives the deterministic elastic modulus.

findings.statement: Junction bending is implemented as `fix restrain` pinned to each junction's as-formed angle (per-junction rest angle avoids the single-rest-angle frustration), with an auto-reduced timestep and an athermal energy-minimised modulus readout.

findings.statement: Bending dominates the mechanics (|E| jumps to tens–hundreds, network no longer floppy) but the modulus is ill-conditioned at v1 size — it scatters and sign-flips across seeds (pathological near-degenerate minima), so it is not yet a calibratable value.
findings.explanation: The stiff, pre-stressed, disordered small network has many near-degenerate energy minima; the equibiaxial-stress modulus is dominated by pre-stress and finite-size buckling rather than the intrinsic shear modulus.
findings.next_action: seed v2: larger network (self-averaging) + pre-stress-free reference

followup_proposals.title: Reproducible bending modulus at scale (larger network + pre-stress-free reference)
followup_proposals.motivation: The bending modulus is ill-conditioned at 200 rods. A 1000+-rod network self-averages the junction disorder, and minimising to a pre-stress-free reference before straining removes the pre-stress artefact — together they should yield a reproducible, positive modulus vs bending_k.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: Self-averaging + a relaxed reference → a well-conditioned shear modulus.

resolved_uncertainties: Bending, not crosslink connectivity, governs this network's stiffness (confirmed qualitatively).
The athermal minimisation measures the floppy modulus deterministically (removes the dynamic-measurement noise).
remaining_uncertainties: A reproducible, calibratable bending modulus — blocked on network size + pre-stress-free measurement.

limitations: Cross-check (2026-10-01): junction bending is NOT a new ingredient — the released code already sets KangNC1=4.0 (@180°) plus two 7S angles. Re-scope as 'match the released angle set', not 'add bending'. See references/cross-check-vs-released-code.md.
Clean-room parameters transcribed from the spec; the authors' LAMMPS input scripts are now public (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20719515) and not yet cross-checked against this build.
The bending modulus is ill-conditioned at 200 rods (pre-stress + finite-size); not calibratable yet.
Bending targets are pinned from a thermally-noisy as-formed geometry (a pre-stress source).
Only equibiaxial stress-strain slope is used; a shear or energy-curvature modulus may be better conditioned.

report.title: Stage v4 — junction bending: the angle-during-assembly fix
report.verdict: Applying the released NC1 bending (k=4.0) via real harmonic angles created as the crosslinks form — matching how the released bond/react templates add angles during assembly — resolves the ill-conditioning: the modulus is positive, reproducible across seeds (36.7/27.6/37.5 LJ) and well-conditioned, where the as-formed restraint sign-flipped. So the released model is not floppy once its angles are faithfully active; the modulus is finite and strongly density-dependent. The remaining gap for an absolute value is matching the make+break crosslink density (the real-angle path runs make-only and over-crosslinks), which needs per-angle deletion or the GCE.
report.main_insight: With the junction angles active during assembly — the way the released model builds them — the network has a reproducible, well-conditioned, finite modulus. The earlier ill-conditioned/soft readings were artifacts of applying bending after assembly (as-formed restraints) and of the angle-off runs. The absolute value now hinges on crosslink density, which the make-only real-angle path over-shoots; matching the released make+break density is the remaining step.
